facts.name: D. Melissa Distler
facts.assignment: Division60, misdemeanor criminal and juvenile delinquency at Kim C. Hammond Justice Center; basic noncivil operating review.

contact.contact_note: Shared judicial office/assistant telephone; no separate personal judicial email established.

hearing_scheduling.summary: Email assistant after filing motion, copying all parties; include case number, motion and requested time. File and serve notice after reservation; notify assistant and file cancellation notice when cancelling.

proposed_orders.summary: Use proposed-order portion of Florida Courts E-Filing Portal; PDF or Word under practices document. Do not email orders unless requested by court.

remote_appearances.summary: Zoom available subject to court instructions. Practices document requests written permission outside arraignments/pretrials; general procedures additionally permit counsel at short non-evidentiary hearings. Confirm applicable authorization; see recorded discrepancy.

chambers_communications.summary: Email assistant with case number/name and subject, copying opposing counsel and self-represented parties; no ex parte communications.

courtesy_copies.summary: Email copies to assistant. General procedures state three business days for memoranda/authorities; practices document states two business days for evidentiary courtesy copies and hearing materials. Both retained.

conferral.summary: General procedures ask parties to try resolving motions and include opposing position. Specialized criminal motion rules were not reviewed.

facts.summary: Email-coordinated hearings, e-portal proposed orders and conditional Zoom appearances. Basic noncivil operating review.

review_scope.collected: Full profile HTML and two PDFs (four and seven pages), with extracted text and acquisition metadata.

review_scope.not_reviewed: Criminal litigation substance, plea forms, trial/exhibit requirements and specialized forms; practices pages6–7 collected without substantive review.

statements.statement: General procedures page3: memoranda and cited authorities at least three business days before hearing.
Practices pages3/5: hearing materials and evidentiary courtesy copies no later than two business days before hearing.

conflicts.resolution: Recorded only; no determination of control.

conflicts.resolution: Recorded only; do not infer blanket permission or October arraignment location.

gaps: Personal judicial email and distinct assistant-only telephone not established.

facts.name: Andrea K. Totten
facts.assignment: Division61 county civil and small claims; profile additionally identifies protective-services, mental-health/substance-use, tuberculosis, firearm-disability and risk-protection matters. Practices document labels Division61 County Civil, Small Claims and Circuit Civil; no general circuit-civil jurisdiction inferred.

office_address: Kim C. Hammond Justice Center, Courtroom402
contact.contact_note: Profile expressly lists no fax. Shared office/assistant telephone; personal judicial email not established.

hearing_scheduling.summary: File motion first and coordinate parties. Use Flagler Benchmark for non-emergency hearings under one hour; scheduling guide also describes four15-minute blocks and directs longer requests to assistant. File notice within24hours and email assistant; contact assistant for cancellations or mistaken reservations.

conferral.summary: Include opposing position in motion; coordinate hearing. Unilateral scheduling only after three unsuccessful attempts on different days at least one day apart, documented in notice.

proposed_orders.summary: File separately through e-portal File Documents on Existing Case to Clerk, unless directed otherwise; do not attach order to motion. Mailing/emailing chambers is not filing. Cover letter optional and separately filed.

courtesy_copies.summary: E-file memoranda/authorities at least two business days before hearing, allowing clerk docketing time; emailed courtesy copies optional and appreciated.

remote_appearances.summary: In-person default. Each participant must separately obtain motion/order permission. File remote request after hearing notice and at least two business days before hearing; notice continues to identify in-person location even if individual permission granted.

chambers_communications.summary: Email assistant with case number and party names; copy all parties except legally authorized ex parte communications.

facts.summary: Benchmark scheduling, existing-case e-portal submissions, optional emailed courtesy copies and participant-specific remote permission. Practical civil operating review only.

facts.name: Sandra C. Upchurch
facts.assignment: Division49 Flagler circuit civil; also Division53 Putnam circuit civil. This review applies Division49 instructions only.

contact.contact_note: Division49 mailbox receives hearing materials and courtesy hearing notices; scheduling/office email uses assistant. Shared office telephone; personal judicial email not established.

hearing_scheduling.summary: Request times from assistant, copying parties, then coordinate and obtain confirmation. File notice within three days of confirmation; email courtesy notice to Division49 mailbox. Cross-noticing requires court permission and party agreement.

conferral.summary: Procedures require Rule1.202 compliance and three attempts including telephone communication, documented in motion when unsuccessful.

proposed_orders.summary: Circulate among parties, then e-file into existing case; ordinarily within seven days after hearing unless directed otherwise. Competing orders not accepted: email assistant for hearing on impasse. Consult official document for formatting and exceptions.

courtesy_copies.summary: Email hearing materials/case law to Division49@circuit7.org; page9 states NO earlier/later than48Hours before hearing and rejects paper copies. Identify hearing date/time/duration and case in subject; wording preserved literally.

remote_appearances.summary: Page3 describes remote non-evidentiary or under60-minute hearings, but separately requires in-person nonjury trials, evidentiary hearings and60-minute-or-longer hearings unless agreed and approved. Confirm format where provisions overlap; requests to attend a designated remote hearing in person require five days notice.

chambers_communications.summary: Email assistant with county, case number/name and relevant matter; copy parties. Do not copy assistant on interparty messages requiring no chambers action. Telephone only if excused from email service.

facts.summary: Assistant-coordinated circuit civil hearings; existing-case e-portal orders; dedicated Division49 hearing-materials mailbox. County-specific and remote-format qualifications retained.

review_scope.content_reviewed: Profile contacts/assignments; PDF pages1–5 office communications, scheduling, conferral, appearance and general proposed-order operations; page9 hearing-materials channel/timing.
review_scope.not_reviewed: Detailed discovery, foreclosure, trial/exhibit and other motion-specific litigation requirements. Putnam procedures and linked trial/notice forms retained as links only.

conflicts.statement: Page3 sectionIII.A uses non-evidentiary matters OR hearings under60minutes for remote proceedings; III.B requires in-person evidentiary and60-minute-or-longer hearings unless agreed/approved. Preserve both; do not infer rule for overlapping categories.
